runs.cmd: T=$($PY mint.py $WORK alg_none); curl -sS -i http://127.0.0.1:27200/v1/messages -H "authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @../wire/request.json | grep -vE '^(Server|Date|content-length):'
runs.out:
HTTP/1.0 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The specified alg value is not allowed"
content-type: application/json

{"error": "invalid_token", "detail": "InvalidAlgorithmError: The specified alg value is not allowed"}

runs.cmd: T=$($PY mint.py $WORK hs256_pubkey); curl -sS -i http://127.0.0.1:27200/v1/messages -H "authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @../wire/request.json | grep -vE '^(Server|Date|content-length):'
runs.out:
HTTP/1.0 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="The specified alg value is not allowed"
content-type: application/json

{"error": "invalid_token", "detail": "InvalidAlgorithmError: The specified alg value is not allowed"}

runs.cmd: $PY mint.py $WORK alg_none | cut -d. -f1 | $PY -c "import sys,base64; s=sys.stdin.read().strip(); print(s, '->', base64.urlsafe_b64decode(s+'='*(-len(s)%4)))"

runs.out: jwt.exceptions.InvalidKeyError: The specified key is an asymmetric key or x509 certificate and should not be used as an HMAC secret.
runs.note: PyJWT will not even create the forgery: it refuses a PEM public key as an HMAC secret
